newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slip, market awaits Irish budget.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slip, market awaits Irish budget.

text.p: Irish government bonds weakened in thin late trade on Monday but not by as much as German bunds which slipped back badly after making good early gains, dealers said.
Analysts said with the German market having posted solid gains much of this month, only fresh evidence of slow German economic growth in data due out later this week could keep the rally going.
"Germany has come back this afternoon, having risen 40 pence from its opening levels in early trade. It has eased on the back of nothing specific at all really," one dealer said.
"We have also come back but not as much. Trade has been thin. At this stage, all eyes are on the budget," the dealer added.
Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn is scheduled to deliver his 1997 budget at 1345 GMT on Wednesday.
He is widely expected to announce tax cuts of around 300 million Irish pounds while analysts expect him to set an exchequer borrowing target of between 600 and 750 million Irish pounds.
By 1625 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 30 pence from Friday's close at 102.95 to yield 5.68 percent having been at 103.05 earlier.
The key benchmark eight percent bond was up 45 pence at 110.35 to yield 6.40 percent, off its earlier high of 110.40.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 78 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 135 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.
"I would see a target of 130 basis points over bunds in the five-year and between 70 and 75 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area," the dealer said.
The U.S. bond market was closed on Monday for Martin Luther King Jr Day, a federal holiday.
